composition.story: One cylinder turns fuel into motion in four strokes: intake, compression, power, exhaust. Step through them and watch the valves, spark, volume and pressure. The crank turns twice, 720°, per cycle. Only the power stroke pushes the piston. The crankshaft's momentum carries it through the other three.

aha.observation: Only the power stroke pushes: burning gas at 60 bar drives the piston down. The other three strokes take energy instead of producing it.

controls.label: Engine state
controls.presentation: Previous / Next buttons. Names stay when disabled. Arrow keys work. Moves one state, 0 to 6. No parameter controls at this depth.

controls.label: Reset to first state
controls.presentation: Goes back to state s1 (intake begins, 0°).

variants.label: Single cylinder, 86 mm bore × 86 mm stroke, 10:1 compression, full throttle

states.label: Intake begins
states.sentence: The piston sits at the top and the intake valve opens, ready to draw in air and fuel.
states.why: Volume equals clearance volume Vc = Vd / (r − 1) = 500 / 9 ≈ 55.6 cc.

states.label: Intake ends
states.sentence: The piston moving down pulls air-fuel mix in until the cylinder is full at bottom dead centre.
states.why: Displacement Vd = π/4 × 8.6² × 8.6 ≈ 500 cc. Full volume = 500 + 55.6 = 555.6 cc.

states.label: Compression
states.sentence: Both valves close and the rising piston squeezes the mix to one tenth of its volume.
states.why: Compression ratio r = 555.6 / 55.6 = 10. Assuming p ∝ r^1.3, pressure ≈ 1 × 10^1.3 ≈ 20 bar.

states.label: Spark
states.sentence: The spark plug fires at top dead centre and the compressed mix burns almost instantly.
states.why: Assumption: burning at nearly constant volume roughly triples the pressure, from 20 to about 60 bar.

states.label: Power stroke
states.sentence: Hot gas pushes the piston down hard, turning the crankshaft. This is the only stroke that produces work.
states.why: Expansion over the same ratio drops pressure about 60 / 10^1.3 ≈ 3 bar. The pressure difference does the work.

states.label: Exhaust
states.sentence: The exhaust valve opens and the rising piston pushes the burnt gas out of the cylinder.
states.why: The crankshaft's momentum, not gas pressure, lifts the piston here.

states.label: Cycle complete
states.sentence: Four strokes take two crank turns, 720°, for one power stroke. Then the cycle repeats.
states.why: Power strokes per crank turn = 1 / 2. At 3000 rpm that is 1500 power strokes per minute per cylinder.

1.reason: The picture of valves, spark, chamber, piston and crank answers "which stroke produces work?", with the piston, chamber and crankshaft highlighted at s5.

2.reason: The scene is step-driven with Previous/Next, so s5 holds until the learner advances, though the aha state shows 3 bar at BDC rather than the 60 bar peak.

3.reason: There is no parameter at this depth, and the fixed 86 mm bore, 10:1 ratio comparison across states is justified; each step changes the active regions and readouts.

4.reason: Valve open/closed values are declared but never bound per state, and s3 highlights both valves as active while the text says they close, so highlights do not trace to a declared state.

6.reason: The rail labels s1 and s2 both "Intake", and s3 and s4 both read 360° although they are named differently, so the labels do not distinguish the events.

7.reason: Each state adds one formula in the why line and a four-item readout, which is a modest density without clutter.
